AIB Data Centers Inc. (AMEX:AIB) shares are trading lower by almost 12% on Wednesday after the company penned a binding agreement with Nebius Group NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) for 50 MW of critical IT capacity at AIB’s data center facility in the southeastern U.S.

• AIB Data Centers stock is showing notable weakness. Why is AIB stock dropping?

Nebius AI Data Center Capacity Contract

AIB expects customer prepayments under the initial 12-year term, along with project-level debt and preferred equity, to cover a substantial portion of the project’s upfront development costs.

The funding structure is expected to reduce AIB’s need for corporate-level common equity and limit potential shareholder dilution.

The capacity is backed by AIB’s previously announced 15-year agreement for 65 MW of utility power at the site, which requires no significant additional electrical infrastructure upgrades. AIB plans to deliver the capacity across two data halls.

The agreement follows AIB’s recent Texas acquisition, which increased its total contracted power capacity to approximately 120 MW.

What AIB Data Centers Does and Why AI Contracts Matter

AIB Data Centers, formerly BlockchAIn Digital Infrastructure, operates in digital infrastructure, providing data center operations and high-performance computing services. It offers power infrastructure, hosting services and equipment leasing to customers tied to blockchain computing, artificial intelligence and high-performance data processing.

The company’s model includes leasing space, power capacity, and equipment within data center facilities, along with modular digital asset mining containers and related hardware and support services. That makes contract announcements around AI data center capacity especially relevant, because they speak directly to utilization, customer demand, and the company’s ability to monetize power and space over time.

AIB Stock Price Action

AIB Data Centers shares were down 12.28% at $1.50 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) stock rose more than 3% Wednesday as chip stocks benefited from strength across the technology sector.

The Nasdaq gained 0.78%, while the S&P 500 rose 0.51%. Technology led all 11 sectors with a 0.97% gain.

Intel has also maintained strong longer-term momentum. The stock has gained about 256% over the past 12 months.

Intel Foundry Gains Ground

Meanwhile, Intel’s foundry business could benefit as artificial intelligence chip customers look for more manufacturing and advanced packaging options beyond Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. (NYSE:TSM).

Counterpoint Research said Intel Foundry revenue rose 31% year over year in the second quarter. That marked the strongest growth among non-memory integrated device manufacturers.

Counterpoint Senior Analyst William Li said Intel and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. (OTC:SSNLF) are benefiting as chip customers seek additional supply sources.

Intel has also gained traction in advanced packaging. Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOG) Google adopted Intel’s EMIB-T packaging technology for its next-generation tensor processing unit, according to Counterpoint.

AI Packaging Could Open Another Growth Avenue

Advanced packaging has become increasingly important as AI accelerators combine multiple compute and memory components.

Counterpoint highlighted Intel’s EMIB packaging technology, along with its ZAM and XBM memory architectures, as potential alternatives to Taiwan Semiconductor’s CoWoS platform.

That could give Intel another path into the AI supply chain as customers seek greater manufacturing diversity and additional packaging capacity.

Still, execution will remain critical. Taiwan Semiconductor continues to hold advantages in scale, production yields and advanced packaging capabilities.

Intel remains above its major moving averages.

The stock is about 9.9% above its 20-day simple moving average of $108.72 and about 48.6% above its 200-day SMA of $80.35.

The 20-day SMA remains above the 50-day SMA, while the 50-day SMA is above the 200-day SMA. That structure points to an established uptrend.

Momentum indicators also remain constructive. The MACD is above its signal line, while the histogram is positive.

Intel is trading closer to the upper end of its 52-week range, which has a high of $142.35.

Resistance sits near $142, just below the 52-week high. Support is near $98.50, close to the psychologically important $100 level.

Earnings And Analyst Outlook

Intel’s next earnings report is estimated for Oct. 22, 2026.

Wall Street expects earnings of 39 cents per share, up from 23 cents a year earlier. Revenue is estimated at $16.41 billion, compared with $13.65 billion a year earlier.

Intel carries a Hold consensus rating with an average price forecast of $114. The forecasts range from $80 to $155 across 50 analysts.

TD Cowen maintained a Hold rating and a $115 price forecast on Sept. 24. Tigress Financial maintained a Buy rating and raised its forecast to $145 on Sept. 15. Piper Sandler initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and a $110 forecast on Sept. 10.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

The Benzinga Edge scorecard currently highlights momentum as the stock’s key measurable strength.

ETF Exposure

Intel is held by several semiconductor-focused ETFs, including the iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX), Invesco Semiconductors ETF (NYSE:PSI) and State Street SPDR NYSE Technology ETF (NYSE:XNTK).

MongoDB Board Authorizes Additional $1 Billion in Buybacks

MongoDB announced that its board signed off on another $1 billion for stock buybacks on Sept. 25. That move lifts the company’s total buyback authorization to $2 billion. Roughly $1.35 billion of that total still remained available as of the filing date.

MongoDB plans to buy shares either on the open market or through privately arranged deals. Market conditions, share prices and management’s own judgment will all shape how quickly the company moves. MongoDB can pause, adjust or end the buyback program whenever it chooses. It also carries no obligation to hit any specific dollar total or share count.

Wall Street Weighs in With Several New Ratings Today

Standard Chartered initiated coverage on a stablecoin-linked token Wednesday, expecting it to outpace both Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) through 2028.

The Token Standard Chartered Is Betting On

Standard Chartered wrote in a September 30 research report that Ethena’s ENA (CRYPTO: ENA) token carries a $2 price target for end-2028, implying roughly 614% upside from the report’s reference price of $0.28. 

The bank ranks Ethena as the fourth-largest stablecoin issuer behind Tether (CRYPTO: USDT), Circle (NYSE:CRCL), and Sky, and notes its USDe stablecoin became the fastest to reach a $10 billion market cap.

Yield-bearing stablecoins currently make up about 5% of the total stablecoin market, and Standard Chartered expects that share to grow as users chase returns alongside stablecoin utility. 

The bank projects USDe’s supply could reach $40 billion by the end of 2028, up from initial reliance on the crypto basis trade, now expanded into real-world assets and equity perpetual futures strategies.

How the Buyback Program Fits In

Ethena’s buyback-and-burn program directs 95% of net revenue toward purchasing and burning ENA tokens. 

Standard Chartered argues a larger USDe supply generates more revenue, which funds larger buybacks, tightening ENA’s supply while demand grows alongside it.

Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE:NVO) on Wednesday revealed new clinical and real-world data at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting, showcasing the efficacy of its next-generation weight-loss treatments.

The presentations highlighted how the investigational drug CagriSema alters brain responses to food, alongside positive real-world outcomes for patients transitioning to oral semaglutide

Read Also: . Tirzepatide or Semaglutide? Novo Nordisk Says Higher Semaglutide Dose Shows Cardiovascular Edge Over Eli Lilly's Tirzepatide

CagriSema Curbs ‘Food Noise’ and Cravings

A 52-week functional magnetic resonance imaging study demonstrated that CagriSema changes how the brain reacts to high-calorie food cues.

The treatment targeted brain regions associated with cravings, reward, behavioral control and sensory processing in overweight and obese adults.

Participants experienced a significant decrease in “food noise,” hunger and appetite. These eating behavior improvements correlated with a 22.4% reduction in body weight compared to a placebo over 52 weeks.

The EASD recognized this research with a Best Abstract Award, emphasizing the drug’s ability to address biological drivers that complicate sustained weight management.

Metabolic Benefits and Clinical Trial Progress

Additional MRI data from the phase 3a REIMAGINE 1 trial showed that early type 2 diabetes patients taking CagriSema experienced notable fat reductions around the liver, pancreas, and abdomen, coupled with a 14.3% weight loss at 40 weeks.

Furthermore, a REIMAGINE 2 post-hoc analysis indicated healthy bone maintenance alongside a 14.2% weight reduction at 68 weeks.

The pharmaceutical company submitted a New Drug Application for CagriSema to the US FDA and Health Canada in December 2025.

In 2026, the firm launched a phase 3 safety and efficacy trial evaluating a high-dose CagriSema formulation in obese adults.

Real-World Data On Oral Semaglutide

The company also shared OCTANE study findings, marking the first real-world data from its collaboration with the telehealth platform Ro.

This research analyzed overweight and obese patients who switched from injectable GLP-1 medications to the once-daily Wegovy pill.

After three months on the oral treatment, users lost an average of 4.1% of their body weight, starting from a 221.6-pound average.

Consequently, the proportion of patients classified as living with obesity dropped from 87.1% to 65.5% in just three months.

Anthropic has hired longtime Google security researcher Ben Hawkes to lead the cybersecurity mission of its Frontier Red Team, adding a veteran vulnerability researcher as AI systems become increasingly capable of carrying out sophisticated cyber tasks.

Hawkes announced the move on X, saying he was joining Anthropic to lead cybersecurity for the Frontier Red Team. He will work alongside the head of the Frontier Red Team, Logan Graham.

"In my career I’ve never seen a clearer opportunity to build a more secure world for everyone. For 40 years we’ve lived with fundamentally insecure technology. What will it take to make the past 40 years of hacking a historical oddity? That’s what I’m here to find out," Hawkes wrote.

Prior to joining Anthropic, Hawkes spent more than 12 years at Google, including nearly seven years as a lead for Project Zero, the company’s security research team known for uncovering vulnerabilities in widely used software and hardware. He later served as an ISE Systems Team Lead before leaving Google in September 2026.

He also founded security research company Isosceles, according to his LinkedIn profile.

Airbnb Adds Social Features and AI Throughout the Booking Process

Airbnb launched a new Connect feature that lets users link with people they know to see past trips, recommendations and upcoming travel plans, displayed on an interactive Travel Map with privacy settings controlling what gets shared. The company also added neighborhood pages summarizing an area’s character, activities and local host experiences.

Airbnb is separately weaving AI into trip planning at nearly every step, starting in the U.S. A new search bar accepts natural language or voice input, AI-powered filters surface related options instantly and listings now come with AI-generated descriptions. Users can compare wishlist homes side by side using AI summaries, and chat support now works in more than 50 languages, with voice support coming soon.

New Services and Host Tools Round Out the Announcement

Airbnb is also broadening its services lineup through the rest of the year, including meal delivery in select European cities, grocery delivery expanding into Europe, and laundry pickup through a partnership with Rinse in select U.S. cities. Starting in November, guests can rent baby gear across more than 60 U.S. cities through a partnership with BabyQuip. The company is also adding local gear rentals, including ski equipment in the French Alps and boats in South Florida.

On the host side, Airbnb plans to roll out several new AI-powered tools later this fall. A multi-listing calendar will let hosts update pricing and availability across listings at once. New 3D floor plans will help guests visualize a home before booking, dynamic pricing recommendations will adjust nightly rates automatically based on demand and an AI earnings dashboard will summarize performance and suggest next steps.

Conagra Brands, Inc. (NYSE:CAG) stock traded lower Wednesday after the packaged-food company beat Wall Street expectations for both earnings and revenue in its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results.

Net sales fell 1.4% year over year to $2.596 billion, beating the $2.589 billion estimate. Adjusted earnings rose 5.1% to 41 cents per share from 39 cents a year earlier, beating the 28-cent estimate.

However, organic net sales fell 1.1%, while adjusted operating margin declined 33 basis points.

Inflation Pressures Margins

GAAP diluted earnings rose 5.9% to 36 cents per share, while net income increased 6% to $174 million. Adjusted net income rose 4.3% to $197 million.

Adjusted operating margin fell 33 basis points to 11.5%, while adjusted gross margin declined 62 basis points to 23.8%.

Productivity gains and $4 million in tariff refunds helped results. However, inflation, lower organic sales and unfavorable operating leverage more than offset those benefits.

Advertising and promotion spending increased 15.1% to $61 million.

Foodservice Outpaces Retail Businesses

Grocery & Snacks net sales fell 2.6% to $1.1 billion, while Refrigerated & Frozen sales declined 2.1% to $1.1 billion.

International sales rose 2.7% to $218 million. Foodservice sales increased 3.2% to $273 million.

Foodservice adjusted operating profit climbed 11.4% to $31 million. Adjusted operating profit declined in Conagra’s other three segments.

Equity-method investment earnings surged 71.8% to $50 million. Conagra attributed the increase mainly to favorable conditions and management of wheat-market volatility at its Ardent Mills joint venture.

Cash Flow Weakens As Debt Falls

Conagra used $4 million of cash in operating activities, compared with $121 million generated a year earlier.

Free cash outflow widened to $128 million from $26 million. Capital expenditures totaled $124 million.

Net debt ended the quarter at $7.4 billion, down $193 million from a year earlier. The company reported a net leverage ratio of 3.99 times.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Conagra Reaffirms Fiscal 2027 Outlook

Conagra reaffirmed fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings guidance of $1.40 to $1.50 per share, compared with the $1.45 estimate.

The company also maintained its forecast for organic net sales to decline 1% to 3% and adjusted operating margin of 10% to 10.5%.

Conagra expects productivity above 4% and plans inflation-related pricing around the middle of the second quarter.

For the second quarter, the company expects organic net sales to decline about 2%. It also sees adjusted operating margin in the high-single-digit range.

Higher logistics and fuel costs, increased advertising spending and the timing of selling, general and administrative expenses are expected to weigh on results.

Consumer Pressure, Freight Costs in Focus

During Wednesday’s conference call, CEO John Brase said the company’s pricing actions were being accepted as planned, with “no surprises” compared with expectations.

Management continues to model roughly 2-to-1 elasticity for the year, including about 1-to-1 in Grocery & Snacks. The outlook does not assume competitors will follow Conagra’s price increases.

Brase also said the consumer is “definitely pressured” and that productivity remains the company’s best tool to limit price increases.

CFO Dave Marberger reiterated expectations for second-quarter organic sales to decline about 2%. Thanksgiving timing and shipments that may run below consumption are expected to weigh on sales.

Conagra said inflation pressures are intensifying, particularly in transportation. Marberger said transportation inflation is running at roughly twice the rate the company had assumed for the year, more than offsetting some relief in protein costs. As a result, Conagra now expects full-year inflation to land toward the high end of its 5% to 6% range.

Rafael Holdings Inc. (NYSE:RFL) stock is trading lower on Wednesday after the company shared topline efficacy and safety findings from its subsidiary Cyclo Therapeutics LLC‘s pivotal Phase 3 TransportNPC study of Trappsol Cyclo in Niemann-Pick Disease Type C (NPC).

The micro-cap biotech company had a market capitalization of about $105.6 million at the previous close, making the stock particularly vulnerable to sharp swings following clinical trial updates.

Trading activity surged as investors reacted to the data. About 1.90 million Rafael shares changed hands during the session, more than 12 times its 100-day average volume of roughly 155,467 shares, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Study Misses Endpoint

While the drug demonstrated a directionally favorable treatment effect by slowing disease progression by 64% at Week 96, the overall primary endpoint did not reach statistical significance.

However, a prespecified subgroup analysis revealed a statistically significant benefit, keeping the drug developer on target for a regulatory filing later this year.

The 96-week trial evaluated 94 patients aged 3 to 70 who received either 2000 mg/kg of intravenous Trappsol Cyclo every two weeks or a placebo.

In a prespecified subgroup representing 83% of participants on background miglustat or leucine therapy, the candidate slowed disease progression by 71% compared to placebo, achieving statistical significance.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

Phase 3 TransportNPC Trial Key Outcomes

The treatment exhibited a well-tolerated safety profile consistent with underlying NPC symptoms.

Treatment-emergent adverse events affected 93.8% of the Trappsol Cyclo cohort versus 100% in the placebo group. Serious treatment-related adverse events occurred at similar rates between the drug group (3.1%) and placebo (3.3%).

Hearing-related events affected 15.6% of treated patients and 13.3% of placebo patients, with one severe case of bilateral deafness reported in the treatment arm.

One patient discontinued treatment early due to an adverse event, and no deaths occurred during the trial.

Safety Profile And Overall Survival Findings

A separate overall survival study compared infantile-onset NPC patients against real-world controls.

Trappsol Cyclo administration correlated with an 85% lower mortality risk compared to matched registry controls. Expanding the historical control cohort to include additional published studies revealed a 94% reduction in mortality risk.

Following a prior pre-NDA meeting with the FDA, the company expects to submit a New Drug Application in the fourth quarter of 2026.

RFL Price Action: Rafael Holdings shares were down 37.89% to $1.26 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

The contract is worth more than $20 billion, according to the Department of Defense, which announced the award on X on Wednesday.

Reuters said the F/A-XX program could eventually be worth hundreds of billions of dollars as production ramps up and potential foreign orders materialize.

The Navy expects the first production aircraft to enter service in the 2030s, operating alongside more than 270 planned F-35Cs, while Super Hornets are expected to remain in service into the 2040s.

What The F/A-XX Contract Covers

The Pentagon said the award covers multiple test aircraft for ground, airworthiness, systems and weapons-integration testing. Pentagon acquisition chief Michael Duffey said, “F/A-XX will dominate contested airspace, extend operational reach, and deliver a decisive combat advantage for the warfighter.”

Boeing’s Second Fighter Win In Two Years

The award follows Boeing’s 2025 win over Lockheed Martin for the Air Force’s F-47, a development contract also worth more than $20 billion.

Boeing Defense CEO Steve Parker said investments in “new facilities uniquely suited to build multiple products with next-generation capabilities” leave the company ready to execute the program.

Delays Give Way To Long-Term Fleet Plan

The Navy competition had faced repeated delays over engineering and supply-chain capacity.

The Pentagon considered pushing the program back by as much as three years before Congress intervened, providing $750 million in 2025 legislation and another $1.4 billion for fiscal 2026.

Lockheed Martin was eliminated from the competition in March 2025, leaving Boeing and Northrop as finalists.

The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge came in below expectations in August. Technical revisions—not easing price pressures—drove the decline.

Annual national accounts revisions from the Bureau of Economic Analysis lowered July headline PCE inflation to 3.4% (from 3.7%) and core PCE to 3% (from 3.3%). Both rates held steady in August, with monthly core PCE rising 0.2%, below the 0.3% consensus.

Traders quickly dialed back rate-hike bets, pushing the odds of an October Fed rate increase down to 37.1% from 70.9% last week, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Economists, however, aren’t so sure.

Much of the Revision Came From Technical Changes

Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, said the downward revision mostly reflects improvements in how computer software and portfolio management fees are measured.

“The changes were well telegraphed and Fed officials will have accounted for most of this already in their outlooks,” Pearce said.

Peter Williams, economist at 22V Research, said the revisions were concentrated in non-market services, prices that are not observed directly in transactions and tend to be noisier.

Consensus expected core PCE at 3.2% after the revisions, according to Williams. The print came in at 3%.

Beyond reducing the odds of an October hike, Williams “wouldn’t place too much emphasis on this print for the Fed.”

One Measure Moved the Other Way

Services prices excluding energy and housing, which the Fed uses to track wage-driven inflation, rose 0.4% in August from 0.1% in July, according to BEA data.

Williams said a narrower version of that measure, which also strips out non-market prices, posted the hottest monthly reading since summer 2022.

“You don’t need your glasses on to tell the difference between 3% core PCE inflation and a 2% target,” Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist at Fifth Third Commercial Bank, said.

Adams added that the Fed wants inflation to fall because price pressures are easing, “not because the way it’s measured changes.”

Growth Was Revised Higher

Real gross domestic product growth in the second quarter was revised up to 2.2% annualized from 1.5%. First-quarter growth was revised to 2.5% from 1.2%, according to Williams.

Pearce said most of the gains came from sectors exposed to artificial intelligence, including IT equipment, data centers and research and development.

Consumers kept spending. Personal spending rose 0.9% in August, while income grew only 0.2%, below the 0.5% consensus. As a result, the saving rate fell to 4.1% from 4.6% in July, the lowest since late 2022, according to Adams.

Meanwhile, ADP reported that private employers added 90,000 jobs in September, above forecasts.

Treasury yields reversed the initial drop after the data.

The two-year yield, the most sensitive to Fed rate expectations, was little changed at 4.89% by early afternoon, while the 10-year rose about 5 basis points to 5.30% and the 30-year about 5 basis points to 5.65%.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (NASDAQ:TLT) fell 0.82% to $77.59 and the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (NASDAQ:IEF) lost 0.32%, while the short-term iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF (NASDAQ:SHY) was flat at $81.18.

Zcash (CRYPTO: ZEC) has surged from roughly $60 to $1,500 over the past year, but Grayscale argues the privacy-focused cryptocurrency may still have room to capture significantly more market share.

The bullish assessment comes as Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan separately identifies privacy, and Zcash specifically, as an emerging long-term crypto narrative that could challenge the sector’s established leaders.

Has Zcash Valuation Hit Ceiling?

On Sept. 29, Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl explained that the magnitude of Zcash’s sharp move can be justified by its low starting valuation and potentially large addressable market.

A year ago, Zcash’s market capitalization represented less than 0.1% of Bitcoin’s (CRYPTO: BTC) and it now accounts for almost 1.5%.

While substantial, Grayscale argues that level is not historically extreme.

XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) is currently valued at nearly 6% of Bitcoin’s market cap, while Bitcoin Cash, Litecoin and Dash each reached at least 3% of Bitcoin’s valuation during the 2017-2018 cycle.

That history suggests Zcash could potentially take additional share without reaching unprecedented relative valuations.

Will Privacy Become Major Crypto Theme?

Hougan’s argument centers less on a specific Zcash price target and more on the broader investment case for privacy developing into a major pillar of crypto adoption.

In an interview with the New Era Finance Podcast on Sept. 29, Hougan said Zcash is making a case that privacy deserves a place among crypto’s most important long-term themes.

He identified Zcash as one of the potential challengers to his existing crypto "Mount Rushmore" of Bitcoin, Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) and Chainlink (CRYPTO: LINK), alongside emerging narratives around Hyperliquid (NASDAQ:PURR), DeFi and AI.

Hougan did not provide a ZEC price target or point to a specific near-term catalyst but stresses on the long-term opportunity of the coin.

For decades, the easiest way to describe the United Arab Emirates to global investors was through one word: oil.

That description is becoming increasingly outdated.

Oil remains critical to the UAE economy, but the country’s investment story is now being shaped by property, tourism, financial services, telecommunications, logistics, technology and infrastructure. Dubai continues attracting international capital and residents, while Abu Dhabi is building its own ecosystem around finance, industry, energy and technology.

The numbers coming from some of the country’s largest listed companies illustrate how quickly that transition is taking place.

Emaar Properties generated AED 49.6 billion in revenue in 2025, up 40%, while property sales reached a record AED 80.4 billion. Aldar Properties reported AED 40.6 billion in group sales, up 21%, while e& increased revenue 23.1% to AED 72.9 billion.

These are not oil companies.

They are businesses tied to the UAE’s expanding population, international capital flows, digital economy and infrastructure spending.

Dubai Is Turning Population Growth Into Economic Demand

One of the most important changes in the UAE is happening at the population level.

The real estate market provides one of the clearest indicators.

Emaar’s 2025 property sales reached AED 80.4 billion, its highest ever, while its revenue backlog climbed 39% to AED 155 billion. The company also controls approximately 618 million square feet of land bank, including around 344 million square feet in the UAE.

The momentum continued into 2026.

During Q1, Emaar’s property sales increased 22% to AED 20.1 billion, while revenue climbed 23% to AED 12.4 billion. EBITDA rose 34% to AED 7.2 billion and net profit before tax increased 33% to AED 7.2 billion. By June, its revenue backlog had reached AED 164.9 billion.

The important point for investors is that Dubai’s property story is increasingly connected to economic migration.

People arriving for employment and business create demand for real estate. Real estate development creates construction activity, while new residents generate spending across hospitality, retail, transportation and financial services.

That creates a multiplier effect that extends well beyond property developers.

Abu Dhabi Is Creating A Different Investment Engine

Dubai gets much of the international attention, but Abu Dhabi is developing a different economic model.

Its strategy combines energy, sovereign investment, financial services, infrastructure, technology and real estate.

Aldar is one of the clearest listed-market examples.

The company generated AED 33.8 billion in revenue during 2025, up 47%, while EBITDA increased 46% to AED 11.2 billion. Net profit rose 36% to AED 8.8 billion.

More importantly, the company’s sales are increasingly international.

Overseas buyers and expatriate residents accounted for 77% of Aldar’s UAE sales in 2025, representing AED 27.4 billion. Its UAE revenue backlog stood at AED 61 billion at the end of 2025.

The trend continued in 2026.

During the first half of the year, overseas and expatriate buyers represented 80% of Aldar’s UAE sales, while its UAE backlog reached AED 59.9 billion. Project-management services backlog stood at another AED 87.2 billion, including AED 62.3 billion of projects under construction.

This is important because it shows that the UAE property market is increasingly linked to international wealth and migration rather than only domestic demand.

Telecom Companies Are Becoming Technology Companies

The UAE’s diversification story also extends into telecommunications.

e& provides a useful example of how an established telecom operator is evolving into a broader technology business.

In 2025, e& generated AED 72.9 billion in revenue, an increase of 23.1%, while net profit increased 33.6% to AED 14.4 billion. EBITDA rose 21.1% to AED 32 billion.

Its subscriber base also expanded sharply.

The group’s consolidated subscribers reached 244.7 million, up 31.3% from 2024. In the UAE alone, subscribers increased 8.4% to 16.3 million.

The significance goes beyond mobile phones.

Telecommunications infrastructure is becoming increasingly important as businesses adopt cloud computing, artificial intelligence, digital payments and connected devices. That creates demand for data centers, cybersecurity, cloud services and enterprise connectivity.

For the UAE, telecom infrastructure can therefore become part of the country’s broader digital-economy strategy rather than simply a traditional utility business.

Tourism Is Adding Another Layer To The Economy

Tourism is another area where the UAE has built a major international advantage.

Dubai’s hospitality, retail and entertainment industries increasingly benefit from the city’s role as a global travel and business hub.

Emaar illustrates this diversification through its recurring businesses.

In 2025, malls, hospitality and leisure generated approximately 32% of Emaar’s EBITDA, reducing the company’s dependence on property development alone. Total EBITDA reached AED 25.6 billion, up 33%.

This matters during different stages of the property cycle.

Property development can produce large but uneven earnings. Hotels, malls and leisure assets can generate recurring revenue from visitors and residents.

The combination creates a business model that is more closely connected to the UAE’s broader economic activity.

Financial Services Are Quietly Becoming More Important

The UAE’s position as a global wealth and business center is also supporting financial services.

Dubai and Abu Dhabi have expanded financial ecosystems to attract international companies, asset managers, family offices and high-net-worth individuals.

This is particularly relevant because international capital is increasingly flowing into UAE real estate and businesses.

Aldar’s overseas and expatriate sales data provide a useful example. If 80% of UAE sales in H1 2026 came from overseas and expatriate buyers, the property market is effectively functioning as an international capital market as well as a domestic real estate market.

The Risks Behind The Diversification Story

The UAE’s transformation does not eliminate risk.

Real estate remains cyclical. Rapid construction, elevated property valuations or a slowdown in population growth could eventually create excess supply.

International capital also creates sensitivity to global interest rates. Higher borrowing costs in the U.S. and Europe can influence property investment decisions and capital flows into the UAE.

Geopolitical risk is another consideration because the UAE sits at the center of a region exposed to conflicts and disruptions in energy and trade markets.

Tourism and aviation are similarly sensitive to regional instability.

There is also a concentration risk within the broader market. Even though the UAE economy is diversifying, hydrocarbons remain an important source of government revenue and national wealth.

Investors therefore should not interpret diversification as meaning the UAE has become completely independent of oil.

Conclusion

The UAE’s economic transformation is becoming visible in the financial results of its largest listed companies.

Emaar’s AED 164.9 billion backlog, Aldar’s AED 59.9 billion UAE backlog, and e&’s AED 72.9 billion of 2025 revenue illustrate three different parts of the same transformation: real estate, infrastructure and digital connectivity.

The UAE still has a significant energy sector.

But its investment opportunity is increasingly being shaped by what happens around that sector.

New residents require homes. Businesses require offices and connectivity. Tourists require hotels and entertainment. International companies require financial services, logistics and infrastructure.

That creates a broader economic ecosystem—and a broader set of listed companies for global investors to analyze.

For investors looking at the UAE today, the more useful question may therefore be not “How much oil does the country produce?” but “How much economic activity can the UAE generate from everything it has built around its oil wealth?”

Pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE:LLY) reported positive data from two late-stage clinical trials, showcasing substantial progress in treatments for both atopic dermatitis and weight management in patients with type 2 diabetes.

Retatrutide Shows Massive Weight Loss Results

The drug manufacturer on Tuesday shared detailed findings from its Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 study for retatrutide, a first-in-class triple hormone receptor agonist targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon.

Over 80 weeks, patients taking the 12-milligram dose shed an average of 49.6 pounds, representing a 20.8% weight reduction.

Participants with a baseline body mass index of 35 or greater lost even more, dropping an average of 60.8 pounds.

Nearly 60% of individuals on the highest dose no longer met the clinical criteria for obesity by the trial’s conclusion.

The experimental treatment also improved blood sugar levels, reducing A1C by up to 1.6%. Up to 40% of users achieved normal blood sugar ranges below 5.7%.

Additionally, retatrutide lowered cardiovascular risk factors, including substantial drops in triglycerides, systolic blood pressure, and waist circumference.

The company intends to file a Biologics License Application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration during the first quarter of 2027.

EBGLYSS Clears Atopic Dermatitis

The Zepbound and Foundayo maker on Wednesday revealed that its EBGLYSS monotherapy achieved both primary and secondary goals at Week 16 in the Phase 3b ADtouch trial.

The drug rapidly improved skin clarity, pain, and itching for adolescents and adults suffering from moderate-to-severe hand and foot atopic dermatitis.

More than 50% of participants saw clear or nearly clear skin by the 16-week mark, with noticeable improvements emerging within a month. Furthermore, patients experienced significant itch relief after just two weeks.

Relying on a newly validated satisfaction scale, nearly eight out of 10 treated individuals reported feeling satisfied or very satisfied regarding their hand skin clearance.
